summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style overview of Ann Arbor, Michigan, covering its college sports (especially the University of Michigan and Michigan Stadium), demographics from the 2010 U.S. Census, local media and colleges, geography and climate, city government, and history from its 1824 founding through the university's arrival in 1837 and the 1960s-70s political activism. It also briefly mentions the city's performing arts groups and the fairy doors installation art downtown.
one_line: Overview of Ann Arbor, Michigan, covering its university-centered sports, 2010 census demographics, media, climate, government, history and arts.
key_facts: Michigan Stadium, the largest American football stadium in the world, was completed in 1927 and cost more than $950,000 to build.
Michigan Stadium has a seating capacity of 109,901 after multiple renovations and is colloquially known as "The Big House".
As of the 2010 U.S. Census, Ann Arbor had 113,394 people, 45,634 households, and 21,704 families.
The population density of Ann Arbor was 4,270.33 people per square mile (2653.47/km²) as of the 2010 U.S. Census.
The Ann Arbor News ended its 174-year print run in 2009 due to economic difficulties and returned to limited print publication under its former name in 2013.
The city's total area is 28.70 square miles (74.33 km2), of which 0.87 square miles (2.25 km2) is water, much of it part of the Huron River.
Ann Arbor is about 35 miles (56 km) west of Detroit.
The elevation ranges from about 750 feet (230 m) along the Huron River to 1,015 feet (309 m) on the city's west side.
The lowest recorded temperature in Ann Arbor was −23 °F (−31 °C) on 11 February 1885, and the highest was 105 °F (41 °C) on 24 July 1934.
Ann Arbor has a council-manager form of government with an 11-member City Council: the mayor and 10 council members.
Christopher Taylor, a Democrat, was elected mayor of Ann Arbor in 2014 and is the current mayor according to the note.
Ann Arbor was founded in 1824 and the University of Michigan moved from Detroit to Ann Arbor in 1837.
Ann Arbor was chartered as a city in 1851, and the Michigan Central Railroad arrived in 1839, making the town a regional transportation hub.
The Ave Maria School of Law opened in Ann Arbor in 2000 and moved to Ave Maria, Florida in 2009; the Thomas M. Cooley Law School then acquired the former buildings as a branch campus.
The University Musical Society, founded in 1879, presents over 60 events each year, and Shakespeare in the Arb has presented one Shakespeare play each June since 2001.
